bookTitle: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets

facts.statement: Because market prices move in wave-like zigzags rather than straight lines, a trend is technically defined by the directional trajectory of successive peaks and troughs. Originating from Dow Theory, an uptrend requires successively higher closing peaks and troughs, whereas a downtrend consists of successively lower closing peaks and troughs.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Market action is characterized by a series of zigzags resembling waves with distinct peaks and troughs. The direction of these peaks and troughs constitutes the market trend [2, 3].

facts.statement: Markets move in three directions: up, down, and sideways. A sideways or trendless market is characterized by horizontal peaks and troughs—referred to in Dow Theory as a 'line'—reflecting a period of price equilibrium where underlying forces of supply and demand are in relative balance.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Sideways / Trendless Trend: Characterized by horizontal peaks and troughs [4, 5]. This reflects a period of price equilibrium where the forces of supply and demand are in relative balance [4].

facts.statement: Prices spend at least one-third of the time in horizontal sideways trading ranges. Because most technical tools and automated trading systems are trend-following by design, they experience severe whipsaws and heavy losses during trendless equilibrium periods, making standing aside the optimal strategic choice over going long or short.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Prices spend at least one-third of the time in sideways trading ranges [4]. Most technical tools and trading systems are trend-following in nature and fail or produce heavy losses during horizontal, trendless periods [6, 7].

facts.statement: Trends operate across three hierarchical time dimensions modeled after ocean movements: Major/Primary trends (the tide) lasting over one year in stocks or over six months in futures; Intermediate/Secondary trends (the waves) lasting three weeks to three months; and Near-Term/Minor trends (ripples) lasting under two to three weeks.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Trends exist across interacting time dimensions and are categorized into three main classifications: Major (> 1 Year Stocks, > 6 Months Futures), Intermediate (3 Weeks to 3 Months), Near-Term (< 3 Weeks) [8-11].

facts.statement: Every trend is simultaneously a component of the next larger trend degree and subdivided into smaller trends, such as an intermediate correction (waves 2-3) within a major uptrend subdividing into minor waves (A-B-C). Intermediate counter-trend corrections typically retrace between 33% and 67% (most frequently 50%) of the prior primary advance.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Each trend is part of the next larger trend and is comprised of smaller trends [14]. Intermediate corrections retrace 33%--67% (often 50%) while near-term trends are used for entry and exit timing [11-16].

facts.statement: Support is a price zone beneath the current market—marked by a prior reaction low—where buying interest is sufficiently strong to overcome selling pressure and turn prices upward. Resistance is a price zone above the market—marked by a prior rally peak—where selling pressure overcomes demand and halts an advance.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Support: A price level or area under the market where buying interest is strong enough to overcome selling pressure, identified by a previous reaction low [17]. Resistance: Selling pressure overcomes buying pressure, identified by a previous rally peak [17, 18].

facts.statement: Support holds on pullbacks because three market cohorts converge to place buy orders: existing longs who regret not buying more initially and add to positions; trapped shorts who sold at the bottom and buy to cover at break-even; and uncommitted traders who missed the rally and wait to enter long on dips.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: The Longs pledge to add to positions if prices dip back to support; The Shorts pray for a price dip back to their break-even entry point to exit; The Uncommitted wait for the next pullback to go long [19, 20].

facts.topic: Determinants of Support and Resistance Significance
facts.statement: The structural strength and predictive authority of any support or resistance zone are governed by three quantitative factors: the duration of time prices spend fluctuating within the congestion area, the total trading volume executed there (reflecting total vested participant commitment), and the chronological recency of the trading activity.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Determinants of Significance: 1. Time Spent: The longer prices fluctuate in a support/resistance area, the more significant it becomes. 2. Volume: Higher trading volume increases importance. 3. Recency: More recent activity has stronger psychological impact [20, 21].

facts.statement: When a support or resistance zone or trendline is decisively penetrated by a significant margin, its technical role reverses. Penetrated support transforms into overhead resistance because trapped longs liquidate on rallies to minimize losses, while penetrated resistance transforms into underlying support on subsequent market pullbacks.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Whenever a support or resistance level is penetrated by a significant margin, they reverse roles [22-24]: Penetrated Support becomes Resistance; Penetrated Resistance becomes Support; Broken up trendlines become resistance [21, 25-27].

facts.statement: To distinguish valid structural breakouts from false intraday spikes and whipsaws, technicians compute the percentage distance between the closing price and the tested boundary. A 3% closing penetration threshold validates breakouts of major support or resistance levels, whereas a 1% threshold validates short-term trading breakouts.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Price Penetration % = |Closing Price - Support/Resistance Level| / Support/Resistance Level * 100%. 3% Rule: Standard benchmark filter for major levels. 1% Rule: Used for short-term levels [28].

variables.definition: Relative percentage distance by which the closing price exceeds the support or resistance threshold
Daily closing price of the asset
Established support or resistance price level being tested

facts.statement: In addition to price percentage filters, technicians apply a temporal confirmation filter known as the 2-Day Rule. To confirm a genuine breakout and filter out single-day exhaustion spikes or false penetrations, the market must register two consecutive daily closes beyond the support or resistance level.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Time Filter (2-Day Rule): Requires two consecutive closes beyond the support or resistance level to confirm a valid breakout [29].

facts.statement: Traders anchor price objectives at major round numbers (10, 20, 25, 50, 75, 100, and 1,000 multiples), causing advances or declines to stall right at these figures. Consequently, buy limit orders must be placed just above round numbers, sell limit orders just below, sell stops below, and buy stops above.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Markets tend to stop advances or declines at major round numbers... Place Buy Limit Orders just above an important round number and Sell Limit Orders just below. Place protective sell stops below and buy stops above key round numbers [30-32].

facts.topic: Round Number Limit Order Execution Example
facts.statement: When targeting a pullback entry near a major psychological round number such as $100.00, placing a buy limit order directly at $100.00 risks non-execution because clustered institutional buying often front-runs the exact level. Traders therefore place buy limit orders slightly above the figure, such as at $101.00, or adjust targets around $99.10.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Buy Limit Orders: Place orders just above an important round number (e.g., 99.10 or 101.00 instead of 100.00) because heavy buying interest at the round figure may prevent the market from reaching it [31].

facts.topic: Historical Gold Market Round Number Barriers
facts.statement: Historical gold price action demonstrates the psychological gravity of century round numbers: the 1982 secular bear market low halted precisely at $300, the subsequent 1983 bull rally peaked just above $500 before retracing exactly to $400 support, and the 1987 advance stalled once again right at the $500 resistance barrier.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Basic Concepts of Trend: Directions, Support & Resistance Psychology
sourceCitation.excerpt: Gold Market Case Study: The 1982 bear market low in gold stopped right at $300. The initial rally in 1983 peaked just above $500 before declining to $400. The 1987 gold rally stalled again at $500 [30].

generalAssumptions: Market action discounts all known and unknown fundamentals.
Prices move in trends, and a trend in motion is more likely to continue than to reverse.
History repeats itself because market support and resistance levels are driven by consistent human psychology of fear, greed, and regret.
